text:
harper: hi team, harper here (started today). I can log into Console but the Flags -> Analytics tab shows "insufficient permissions". Who's the right contact to get staging analytics/viewer access?

onboard-buddy: welcome @harper! :wave: usually infra grants the analytics role via Okta group `redwood-console-analytics-staging`. If you want faster help ping @maya_ops or file an access request.

harper: filed the form but it says pending. I'm trying to pull flag evaluation metrics for a quick spike analysis for my onboarding project. email is harper@redwood.com.

maya_ops: welcome! I'll check the request. For staging we can do a manual add (reads only) for 14 days. For prod analytics it's stricter (security review + signed NDA sometimes). Do you also need a service account to pull metrics programmatically?

harper: yes — a read-only SA for the metrics job would be great. Planning to run some local Jupyter queries against staging only.

security: tagging from security 14: Hey Harper, for read-only metrics we usually allow `analytics.read` and `flags.metrics` scopes for staging. Make sure the notebook doesn't store keys in public repos. For programmatic access, we put SA in Vault and issue a 7-day lease by default. If you need longer, include justification in the access request.

maya_ops: created ticket ACC-9201. Approvers: manager + infra. Manual quick-add queued. If you need the SA created now, reply here with your notebook repo and job name.

harper: repo: github.com/redwood/harper-playground, job: notebook:flag-metrics. I attached manager @laura to the access request.

onboard-buddy: small tips: 1) enable 2FA before infra approves, 2) if group add seems slow do a full logout/login (Okta token refresh). Okta sync sometimes takes ~5-10m.

maya_ops: creating SA now with tags `analytics-read` + `notebook-staging`. We'll place key in Vault path `secret/onboarding/sa/harper-analytics` and give you a 7-day read lease. Manual group add in progress.

devex-bot: Docs link: https://docs.redwood.com/onboarding/console-analytics. Note: ffctl metrics commands exist for quick pulls (example below).

harper: can you paste the ffctl examples?

devex-bot: sure. Example snippet you can add to your notebook:
```
# get SA key from Vault
vault read -field=value secret/onboarding/sa/harper-analytics > /tmp/sa.json
# login
ffctl auth login --service-account=/tmp/sa.json
# pull flag evaluation metrics
ffctl metrics list --env=staging --flag=my_feature --since=24h
```
maya_ops: manual grant completed by maya_ops. Group added: `redwood-console-analytics-staging`. SA key deposited in Vault.

harper: confirmed I can open Analytics and run the ffctl metrics command. one more Q: how often do the metrics exports refresh and is there a TTL on historical data in staging?

security: metrics pipeline in staging retains 30 days by default. If you need longer-term exports we can help schedule a periodic export to a secure bucket (requires a second approval for external storage).

harper: got it, that's fine for now. I'll add a short how-to to onboarding docs and link the notebook examples. thanks, everyone! :tada:
